t: Daoism grew from the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi, works of the Warring States period which taught harmony with the Dao, the Way underlying all things, through simplicity, spontaneity and effortless action.

From 142 CE, with the Way of the Celestial Masters, it became an organised religion of priests, rituals, scriptures and gods, seeking long life and transcendence, and emperors, above all the Tang, who claimed Laozi as their ancestor, patronised it.

It shaped Chinese medicine, painting, poetry, alchemy and the martial arts, survived the persecutions of the 20th century, and its classic, the Daodejing, is one of the most translated works in world literature.
dyk: The earliest known description of a gunpowder-like mixture comes from a Daoist alchemical text of about the mid-9th century, which warns that heating saltpetre and sulphur with honey has burnt alchemists’ hands and faces and even their houses.
ev: Bamboo slips buried in a tomb at Guodian preserve the oldest known passages of the Daodejing
Zhang Daoling receives a revelation from the deified Laozi and founds the Way of the Celestial Masters
The Yellow Turban rebellion of the Way of Great Peace shakes the Han dynasty
The Northern Wei emperor Taiwu receives Daoist registers, making Daoism the religion of his state
The Tang emperor Gaozong honours Laozi, the dynasty’s claimed ancestor, as an emperor
Wang Chongyang founds the monastic school of Complete Perfection (Quanzhen)
The Quanzhen master Qiu Chuji meets Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush
The Ming court completes the printing of the Daoist Canon

f.origin: China, as a philosophy in the Warring States period (4th–3rd centuries BCE) and as an organised religion from 142 CE
f.founder: Laozi, by tradition the author of the Daodejing; Zhuangzi; Zhang Daoling, the first Celestial Master
f.scriptures: The Daodejing and the Zhuangzi; the Daoist Canon (Daozang), printed in 1445 and 1607, with some 1,500 texts
f.followers: Hard to count: Daoist priests and monastics serve temples in China, Taiwan and Chinese communities abroad, and its practices reach many millions more
